issues.claim: This round's VRC5T-05 fix gives §11.2's `LooksAnswer.crises[].over` (l. 16440) the clause 'absent on every look where the model the view draws holds no building at the query's building, or no field at its field (an address it lacks, or one of another kind), every other member as without it — never an error (V10 §3.23 row 34)'. As written, a query whose `building` names no building leaves `over` off every look. That includes the famine looks, even when the query's `field` names a field a famine draws bare. Likewise a `field` naming no field blanks a valid building's disaster `over`. V10 §3.23 row 34 (l. 2733), which cites this comment as its home, composes the two members by look kind: 'a read asked with both a building and a field → each disaster look's `over` as asked with the building alone and each famine look's as asked with the field alone'. Take a read whose building is a district and whose field is a field a famine draws bare. V10 gives the famine look `over` true; §11.2 gives it no `over`. V10's §3.5 pass-through hands both members to §11.2's query, so the clerk's answer depends on which text the builder of `looks` follows. That is two units stating two outcomes for one case, which R6-01 grades MAJOR however rare the case. The ambiguity is in my round-5 required change ('absent on every look where the query's building names no building, or its field no field'), which the repair wrote as given. T-ER-27's new input, with both members naming nothing, has one outcome under either reading, so no bar tells the builds apart.
issues.required_change: §11.2's `over` comment: 'absent on every look where the model the view draws holds no building at the query's building, or no field at its field (an address it lacks, or one of another kind), every other member as without it — never an error (V10 §3.23 row 34)' → 'absent on each disaster look where the model the view draws holds no building at the query's building, and on each famine look where it holds no field at its field (an address it lacks, or one of another kind) — each look kind read from its own member alone, every other member as without them — never an error (V10 §3.23 row 34)'. T-ER-27's input, after 'a `looks` query whose building names a district and whose field names a plot', adds '; one whose building names a district and whose field names a field a famine look draws bare'. Its outcome, after '`over` absent on every look, the rest as without them', adds '; `over` absent on each disaster look and true on the famine look'. V10's row 34 stands, since it already composes by look kind.

issues.claim: §11.2's `ExportOpts.pins` (l. 16323–16329), written this round for VAT-r5-02, draws each view pin as 'a numbered marker in its colour at its point' and each public note as 'a numbered marker at its thing's anchor'. It numbers them 'from 1, the view pins in the view section's order, then the public notes in their things' address order, the numbers keyed on §9.5's separate legend sheet'. It leaves out only 'a public note on a thing the export's knowledge withholds'. Two common cases have no outcome. (a) A view pin, or a note's anchor, outside the export's frame. V09 §5.10 (l. 4071) frames a picture as the current view, the whole town or a district, so a picture of an annotated map usually has pins outside its frame. (b) A public note whose thing the model the export draws lacks: a building an epoch demolished before the export's drawn week, or one built after it (§4.11 *Which week is drawn*). The note stays in the view section (V09 §4.19). Builders can split three ways. One numbers and keys every pin and note, so the legend sheet lists markers the picture lacks and the drawn numbers skip. Another numbers only what it draws. For (b), a third draws the note at its thing's head anchor, where the picture holds no such thing, or fails on the missing anchor. §9.5's *Annotation layer* (l. 15168) is silent. T-ER-19 (l. 16906) runs only pins and notes inside the frame on things that stand. This is an edge on a normal path with no defined outcome (principle (11)), and the builds give different picture bytes.
issues.required_change: `ExportOpts.pins`' comment, after 'a public note on a thing the export's knowledge withholds left out (§11.1 *Knowledge*)', adds '; a view pin whose point lies outside the export's frame, and a public note whose thing the model the export draws lacks at its drawn week (§4.11 *Which week is drawn*) or whose anchor lies outside the frame, left out likewise — the numbers counting only the markers drawn, from 1 with no gap, and the legend sheet keying those alone'. T-ER-19's input, after 'and holding a public note on a building, one on a way and one on a building the export's key withholds', adds ', a view pin outside a district picture's frame and a public note on a building demolished before the export's drawn week'. Its outcome, after 'the withheld building's note left out', adds ', the outside pin and the demolished building's note left out, the drawn markers numbered 1 to n with no gap and the legend sheet keying those alone'.

issues.claim: §8.2's `StyleSheet.groups` (l. 12601), written this round for VAT-r5-04, defines more than the switch itself. 'absent, or a member absent, true'; 'kept under a viewer's `stylePreset` as the document's rows are (§11.3)'; 'a group switched off draws none of its marks — no shadow cast, no surface written, no hit — and a picture draws what the style draws'. The only bar for the switch is T-V1-56 (c) (R6-10): 'the `pins` and `trees` group switches each run: the group hidden, logged as one `setStyle`, undone, the model digest unchanged'. No bar in §8.11, §11.6 or any volume runs the shadow, surface, hit, picture or preset outcome, or a sheet without `groups`. §8.4's light pass reads trees as casters and surface writers from §8.10's instances, apart from the display list's marks. So a build that hides the group's marks while tree shadows stay drawn passes every bar. So does a build where a hidden pin still answers a click, or where a viewer's preset brings the groups back. The switch is a toggle, which principle (11) names. R6-01 grades a defined outcome that no bar runs, so that a wrong build passes every bar, MAJOR (a bar that passes a wrong result).
issues.required_change: §8.11 adds a row after T-ER-29: '| T-ER-30 | the drawing-group switches (§8.2's `StyleSheet.groups`; §8.4's *Toggles are visibility*) at every rung THORP to the cap: `trees` off and `pins` off, each alone and together, in a lit view by day and by night; the same under a viewer's `stylePreset` of another family; a picture export; a click on a hidden pin's point and on a hidden tree's crown; a sheet saved without `groups`, and one with a member absent; save, load, undo, redo, regenerate and migrate | none of the group's marks drawn, no shadow cast and no surface written by them, no hit on them, the click reaching what lies beneath; the export without them; the same under the preset; both groups drawn; that member's group drawn; each lifecycle step drawing what its style holds, the model digest unchanged — never an error | a lit CITY view and its PNG export with each group off: 0 of its marks, shadow pixels, surface samples or hit entries in the view, under the preset and in the export; the sheets without `groups` drawing both groups; from the milestone that lands V01 §5.1.3's group switches |'.

issues.claim: §8.2's new `StyleSheet.groups` comment (l. 12601) keeps the drawing-group switches 'under a viewer's `stylePreset` as the document's rows are (§11.3)'. §11.3 (l. 16815–16817), the home it cites, lists what survives a preset: 'the chosen preset replaces the document's sheet for that viewer only, and the document's own rows (thematic overrides, ground-cover regions) apply on top where the preset has the roles they name'. That list omits `groups`. §8.9's raster-export request (l. 14554) reads 'the viewer's `stylePreset` sheet with the document's rows, §11.3'. §8.2 states the rule itself, so nothing built or tested changes. The defect is a list that omits an item its own rule names.
issues.required_change: §11.3: 'and the document's own rows (thematic overrides, ground-cover regions) apply on top where the preset has the roles they name' → 'and the document's own rows (thematic overrides, ground-cover regions) apply on top where the preset has the roles they name, and its drawing-group switches (`StyleSheet.groups`, §8.2) apply whatever the preset'.
